{{Otheruses|Blaster}}
{{Citation}}
[[File:E11BlasterRifle-NEGWT.png|thumb|250px|The popular [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]]-issue [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]] [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]]]]
{{Quote|Hokey religions and ancient weapons are no match for a good blaster at your side.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] on the supposed advantages of a blaster over a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]|<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''blaster''', also called a '''gun''', was a ranged weapon that fired bursts of [[Particle beam/Legends|particle beam]] energy called ''blaster bolts'' from a replaceable [[Blaster power pack/Legends|power pack]]. The most commonly used weapon in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], blasters' intense beams consisted of compacted high-energy particles and intense light that could kill or paralyze their target, depending on the setting. Blasters ranged in size and power from compact [[Blaster pistol/Legends|pistols]] to large, heavy [[Blaster rifle/Legends|rifles]] to [[Starship/Legends|starship]]-mounted [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]]. Some beings used blasters from their youth: [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] owned a small [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blaster]] in his childhood, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] was given a [[Sporting blaster/Legends|sporting blaster]] when she was a teenager, and [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] children were given blasters, along with extensive training, prior to becoming thirteen standard years old. Throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] usually held a blaster rifle if not any type of specialist.

==Name==
The terms ''blaster'' and [[Laser/Legends|''laser'']] were often used interchangeably in everyday conversation, both denoting the same type of particle beam weapon. However, technically speaking, the laser was a much older weapon design than the blaster, and blasters' firing cycles had faster recharge rates than those of lasers, allowing them to attain a much higher rate of fire, though at a loss of range and accuracy.

A blaster could also be referred to as a "gun".<ref name="Rookies">{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}</ref>

There was some dispute as to what size of weapon the term ''blaster'' denoted. For example, blasters were commonly thought of as handheld weapons only, but starship-mounted blaster cannons could fall into this category as well.

==Blaster mechanics==
===Operation===
{{Quote|An old trick...<br />...that always works|[[Kir Kanos]] destabilizes a blaster pistol, creating a makeshift [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]]|<ref name="Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 3">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 3|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:Blaster_bomb.jpg|thumb|left|360px|A blaster pistol. Here, the device is being rigged to explode.]]
Instead of firing a coherent beam of light like the archaic laser, the blaster fired a compressed, focused, high-energy particle-beam that was very destructive, commonly referred to as a "bolt". Generating the bolt relied on two components: a gas cartridge filled with an energy-rich [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]] (typically [[Tibanna/Legends|Tibanna]]) and a [[Blaster power pack/Legends|power pack]]. When the blaster was fired, a small amount of gas moved from the cartridge through the [[Heter-Valve|Heter valve]] into the gas conversion enabler chamber, commonly called the [[XCiter/Legends|XCiter]]. In this chamber, the power pack energized the gas, before it passed into the [[Actuating module/Legends|actuating blaster module]], where the now extremely high-energy gas was transformed into a compressed beam of intense energy particles, coupled with intense light. The particle beam was then focused through a [[Prismatic crystal/Legends|prismatic crystal]] or a similar device, which generated a deadly high-energy particle beam, fired from the emitter nozzle as a bolt of glowing energy. The color of the bolt depended on the gas used and the type of focusing device, and could vary from red to blue to orange to white.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref><ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

A side effect of firing blasters was the gas conversion enabler heating up as gas was energized by the power pack, which could cause blasters to overheat, sometimes to the point of destruction. Additionally, a small amount of [[Ozone/Legends|ozone]] was emitted as a trace product of the bolt emerging from the emitter nozzle, lending blaster bolts a distinctive smell that [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] characterized as being like burnt meat.<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref>

===Ammunition===
[[File:Deflecting_Slash_JATM.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Blasters fired bolts of energy.]]
Most personal blasters had two kinds of ammunition: a gas cartridge and a power cell. Blaster gas cartridges could typically provide for up to five hundred shots before needing replacement. Most blaster power packs could supply energy for up to one hundred shots. Certain more powerful weapons put greater demands on the gas cartridge, power pack, or both: less powerful weapons, like the [[Drearian Defense Conglomerate/Legends|Drearian Defense Conglomerate]] [[Defender sporting blaster pistol/Legends|Defender sporting blaster pistol]], relied largely on the power cell and used only a small quantity of gas, while very powerful weapons, such as the illegal [[Disruptor/Legends|disruptor]], used much larger amounts of gas. Still other weapons, namely those dating from earlier times, employed a kind of removable power cell/cartridge which supplied enough energy (though at weaker levels) to make total expenditure seldom. Most blasters also had a [[Stun/Legends|stun]] setting, which fed power through a secondary emitter, bypassing the gas chamber to create a ring-shaped electromagnetic burst that disrupted the target's [[nervous system]], often leaving them unconscious.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Blaster bolts themselves carried no heat. On impact, however, their displacement of matter produced kinetic energy that caused heat: the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] was displaced by the bolt's passage (causing the blaster's iconic sound<ref name="RCHC">''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''</ref>); materials struck by bolts tended to deform and fuse, and liquids inside organic bodies instantly changed state to steam, expanding and doing terrible damage to surrounding tissue.<ref name="TEGTW" /> Consequently, bolts usually dissipated in a small, but violent, explosion of extreme heat and force upon contact with an unshielded surface, sometimes leaving blast points. Weapons such as Han Solo's [[DL-44 heavy blaster pistol/Legends|DL-44 heavy blaster pistol]] and the [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]] could cause incredible destruction, and had the power to blow large chunks from stone walls and smaller holes and pockmarks out of durasteel bulkheads, as seen in Han Solo and Luke Skywalker's [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|raid]] on [[Detention Block AA-23/Legends|Detention Block AA-23]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Episode I" />

==History and usage==
{{Quote|So uncivilized.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], after killing [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] with the latter's own weapon|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:Rakatan_blaster.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The earliest known type of blaster.]]
The oldest known weapon that could be called a blaster was used by an [[Rakatan guardian droid|ancient droid]] of an unknown model employed by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. This weapon was considered to be extremely up-to-date compared to the blasters of the year [[3956 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

The first blasters developed by the greater galaxy were reverse-engineered from Rakatan technology after the collapse of the Infinite Empire. These were heavy [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]] weapons that combined large energy conductors with huge power generators. These early blasters were destructive but were slow to fire, temperamental, and difficult to move. As more efficient energy sources were developed, blasters became smaller and more practical, becoming anti-infantry emplacements and then handheld weapons known as ''[[Beam tube/Legends|beam tubes]]''. These consisted of backpack power generators with a hose coming out of the side that connected to a handheld focusing tube. All of the equipment that created the blaster beam was contained in the backpack and was fired through the hose. The beam tube was the dominant weapon of the elite infantry of [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]], the [[Duinarbulon Star Lancers]], around [[25,130 BBY]] and came to displace [[heatbeam]]s and [[Plasma cannon/Legends|plasma cannons]] (both of which used [[Laser/Legends|lasers]] to heat [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]]) because they were safer to carry and required less maintenance.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Beam tubes were replaced by ''[[pulse-wave blaster]]s'' in [[7811 BBY]]. These weapons produced a more powerful beam and had a much greater rate of fire. The pulse-wave weapons of [[Waymancy Hollow]] dramatically overpowered the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Waymancy Storm]] conflict until the Republic was able to reverse-engineer the [[Sif-Alulan process]] to produce pulse-wave blasters of its own.<ref name="Author's Cut 4">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-4-the-rise-of-the-republic-needs-author-entry|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 4: The Rise of the Republic}}</ref>

The next innovation in blaster technology was the ''[[Triple blaster/Legends|triple blaster]]'', which dated to the early Galactic Republic. It worked by using three separate weapons connected to the same targeting system, often coordinated in sets of two or four and fired simultaneously at a target. Triple blasters had become exceedingly rare by the [[Rise of the Empire era|rise of the Empire]]. Pulse-wave weapons were still in extensive use at the time of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] around [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], but lost out to the triple blaster as they were imprecise and lacked range.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Further developments in the lead up to the [[Mandalorian Wars]] led to the decline of triple blaster technology as what is traditionally thought of as ''the blaster'' was created: a self-contained unit that could produce bolts by itself with no additional equipment. Blasters were a mature technology from this point, and blasters from the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] were considered identical in operation to their successors from the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] twenty years later.<ref name="TEGTWAT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

[[File:Hans_Heavy_Blaster_Pistol_EoD.png|thumb|right|200px|Han Solo used a DL-44 heavy blaster pistol.]]
Blasters rapidly displaced the [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] as the primary infantry weapon owing to their greater ammunition capacity and power, and lighter ammunition than [[Slug/Legends|slugs]]. However, slugthrowers were still more useful than blasters in certain environments, such as exceptionally humid locales like jungles, which might destroy a blaster's delicate internal components.<ref name="Shatterpoint">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref> Slugthrowers could also be silenced more easily than blasters and did not produce a visible bolt.

An updated version of blaster technology developed during the Clone Wars were ''"stealth" blasters'', exemplified by the [[DC-19 "Stealth" carbine]] used by the Republic's [[Clone shadow trooper/Legends|clone shadow troopers]]. The DC-19 had a sound-suppressor unit that allowed the user to operate the blaster in virtually complete silence, and also had an alternate stealth firing mode that used a refined mixture of tibanna gas, making the bolt invisible to the naked [[Eye/Legends|eye]]. However, the invisible tibanna mix had to be reloaded after every ten shots, and there was a required cool-down [[Time/Legends|time]] between each shot to protect the blaster's dampeners from overheating. A further development of this was the [[Nightstinger sporting blaster rifle]]. Another development during the Galactic Civil War was the ''[[autoblaster]]''. Designed for the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]], it had a higher rate of fire than other blasters, but did not become commonly available until after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

The most common personal weapon in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by the rise of the Empire, blasters were often used not only by military personnel, but by civilians as protection. They were more commonly seen in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] worlds, though small, concealable [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blasters]] were frequently used by social elite, such as Baron Administrator [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]. Many establishments, such as the [[Cantina/Legends|Cantina]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], had restrictions against use of blasters, though these were often overlooked if the conflict remained small.

The most common manufacturer of blasters during the Galactic Civil War was [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]], which had contracts with both the Imperial Military and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. It also manufactured the ''Protector'' civilian fighter-grade blaster line as well as the E type, such as the [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]] used commonly by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and later by a semi-major pirate faction called FTS, most of which was salvaged after the end of the Galactic Civil War.

==Blaster accessories==
Many blasters had attachments and accessories to aid in targeting, accuracy, rate of fire, and grip. Attachments included [[Targeting laser/Legends|targeting lasers]], [[Rangefinder/Legends|electronic scopes]], and larger power packs. [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad's]] [[DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System/Legends|DC-17m]] interchangeable blasters had sniper and anti-armor attachments for adaptability in unpredictable situations. [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett's]] [[EE-3 carbine rifle/Legends|EE-3 carbine rifle]] had a small scope which could interface with Fett's helmet for increased accuracy. [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett's]] two [[WESTAR-34 blaster pistol/Legends|WESTAR-34 blaster pistols]] had [[Dallorian alloy/Legends|dallorian alloy]] plating, which kept the weapon from overheating. [[Clone trooper/Legends|Clone troopers']] [[DC-15A blaster rifle/Legends|DC-15A blasters]] could interface with their helmets.
